Visit Smoke Signals x Reflections, an exhibition where photography, beadwork, sculpture and digital media serve as a guiding signal, broadcasting stories of identity, memory and reconnection. 

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.
 
Smoke Signals x Reflections is a safe and affirming space for two-spirit, Indigi-queer, and gender nonconforming artists.

Presenting the work of 5 women artists who meet monthly to share their work. 

The isolation of individual art practice is counter-balanced by their association with each other. Working in different media, the sensibility and leanings of each artist inform and enrich, while each remain very particular in their vision. Each artist moves individually between representation and abstraction, between internal and external, offering consistently thoughtful observation, detailed wonder and worry, and determination to question the work, its context in art, in the social and cultural realm, and in the spheres larger and smaller.

value.event_description:
Showcasing photography by Ryan Bolton and Yuma Dean Hester!

With no fixed itinerary, we traveled north through Northern Alberta into the Rockies. We then ventured into the Yukon and the Northwest Territories in pursuit of the Northern Lights. What began as a road trip became an exercise in listening and being present.

Along the way, we met with Elders, Chiefs, and storytellers whose histories are inseparable from the land. Conversations about memory, responsibility, and continuity, reminders that these landscapes are not empty expanses, but living territories shaped by generations of knowledge and care.

Before Borders reflects on what it means to cross provincial lines while recognizing deeper, enduring boundaries that predate them. The work considers travel not as an escape, but as an exchange, guided by those who have called this land home since time immemorial.

By Keith Alessi, this is a charming, autobiographical story of passion, art, and resilience. 

Neither an actor nor a musician by trade, Keith was faced with a major cancer battle and, in the wake of his brush with mortality, chose to leave the world of corporate boardrooms behind to follow his long-delayed passion: playing the banjo. It was a pursuit that would ultimately help save his life. 

Keith is now on a mission to raise money for causes close to his heart and is donating his performance and all proceeds from the event, directly to support Studio 180 Theatre’s ongoing work fostering compelling conversations on stage, in the classroom, and in the community.

The debut of an exciting new Canadian play.

On the deck of a ship stands ‘The Atlantean,’ a single-seat submersible designed to withstand the deepest reaches of Earth’s oceans. Next to it stands Levin, whose dream of a research mission to the bottom of the ocean has become a reality in spite of questions surrounding his scientific views. The deeper he goes, and the darker it gets, the more dire his dive becomes, and the surer he gets that he is being stalked by something just out of sight…

A story of wonder, fear, and romance, this is the story of a scientist’s descent into a world where he will either shed light on one of the world’s last great mysteries, or become a part of it.

Enjoy the world premiere of Karma by Aksam Alyousef, directed by Ash Knight, starring Basel Daoud, Zaynna Khalife, Andrew Iles, Tony Nash, and Christina Tannous. 

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. His Syrian mother, Karma, worries for his mental health, and forces him to dismiss the notion. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

How well can you read handwritten items? Come test your decoding skills as we explore several hundred years of handwritten words on items from Toronto Public Library’s Special Collections. 

The value of cursive writing has become a matter of debate as rapid technological changes make the need to put pen to paper increasingly rare. 

One area where the prominence of handwriting is undeniable is in archives of historical papers - explore this exhibition and see a variety of formats that researchers make use of such as personal letters, diaries, and notebooks as well as public documents, business records, and maps.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections. 

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

Moving between fantasy and reality, past and present, and inspired by equine therapy, the play explores the deepening bond between a Horse and a Woman, and how they come together to negotiate their relationship, re-discover play and how they eventually heal each other in the process.

A high octane rollercoaster with stunning visuals and immersive soundscape, this experience is for anyone seeking a silver lining in the dark.

Enjoy the world premiere of Karma by Aksam Alyousef, directed by Ash Knight, starring Basel Daoud, Zaynna Khalife, Andrew Iles, Tony Nash, and Christina Tannous. 

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. His Syrian mother, Karma, worries for his mental health, and forces him to dismiss the notion. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

The debut of an exciting new Canadian play.

On the deck of a ship stands ‘The Atlantean,’ a single-seat submersible designed to withstand the deepest reaches of Earth’s oceans. Next to it stands Levin, whose dream of a research mission to the bottom of the ocean has become a reality in spite of questions surrounding his scientific views. The deeper he goes, and the darker it gets, the more dire his dive becomes, and the surer he gets that he is being stalked by something just out of sight…

A story of wonder, fear, and romance, this is the story of a scientist’s descent into a world where he will either shed light on one of the world’s last great mysteries, or become a part of it.

A plea and guiding map for humanity, expressed in music. 

Enjoy the Upper Canada Choristers and their accomplished Latin ensemble Cantemos as they premiere Common Ground, a 6-movement cycle written for them by their music director, Laurie Evan Fraser. 

The new work is dedicated to the insightful and widely followed U.S. historian Heather Cox Richardson, who advocates for “art as joyful resistance”. The music features settings of poetry in English by Jacqui Atkin and in Spanish by Jacinto Salcedo.  With the instrumental participation of the choir’s pianist Hye Won (Cecilia) Lee and guest oboist Karen Ages. 

Including songs on the theme of empathy and understanding by Broadway composers Richard Rodgers, Lerner and Lowe, and others. Cantemos sings Venezuela’s energetic unofficial national anthem, Alma llanera (Soul of the Plains).

Classical music and jazz collide as two of today’s most prolific and compelling pianists join forces to create a unique program featuring jazz exploration, classical romanticism, and pop allure.

Grammy Award-winning jazz pianist Brad Mehldau has recorded and performed extensively since the early 1990s. He is first and foremost an improviser and greatly cherishes the surprise and wonder that can occur from a spontaneous musical idea that is expressed directly, in real time. But he also has a deep fascination for the formal architecture of music, and it informs everything he plays. The two sides of Mehldau’s personality – the improviser and the formalist – play off each other, and the effect is often something like controlled chaos. 

Kirill Gerstein has established himself as one of today’s most prolific and compelling performers.

David Bradstreet came to Canada from England with his parents and sister in 1956. After studying architecture he played the Campus Directions college coffeehouse circuit in the U.S. and for three years visited most states as a solo performer. He spent pivotal time in New York City working with Peter Yarrow (of Peter, Paul and Mary) and Phil Ramone including a duo with Mimi Farina. He joined Lazarus (with Carl Keesee and Billie Hughes), worked with Albert Grossman in Woodstock NY and toured with Todd Rundgren.

Returning to Canada, David’s song, Renaissance, became a folk standard. The late '70s produced two high profile albums “David Bradstreet” and “Dreaming in Colour”, which led to the JUNO for Best New Male Vocalist 1977.

Major tours ensued (Supertramp, John Prine, etc.), with concert and broadcast appearances including Ian Tyson’s Nashville North.

Special guests including renowned flamenco dancer/choreographer Jose Manuel Álvarez (Barcelona, Spain) and celebrated singer Manuel Soto (Jerez, Spain), join the award-winning company for a vibrant, emotionally charged performance.

Armonía is about artists who are deeply connected to what they do, moving with the rhythm, energy, and emotion of the music. At its core is the idea of harmony: the way elements come together to create a sense of balance and unity. This harmony extends beyond the stage, reflecting how we experience connection in our own lives.

From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

How well can you read handwritten items? Come test your decoding skills as we explore several hundred years of handwritten words on items from Toronto Public Library’s Special Collections. 

The value of cursive writing has become a matter of debate as rapid technological changes make the need to put pen to paper increasingly rare. 

One area where the prominence of handwriting is undeniable is in archives of historical papers - explore this exhibition and see a variety of formats that researchers make use of such as personal letters, diaries, and notebooks as well as public documents, business records, and maps.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

value.event_description:
In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

fields.alt: Two women float in the water, one above the other.

value.event_description:
Emerge from winter hibernation and welcome in the spring energy this May. Explore the elements (Earth, Fire, Water & Air) through an open level vinyasa yoga flow and sound-bath meditation in a four-week series. Join Keke Chambers, a multi-disciplinary artist, facilitator, and healer with over two decades of movement experience. Each week you’ll explore the elements by infusing movement with connection to each week’s theme. With an emphasis on accessibility and inclusion, you’ll be guided to connect to your own inner teacher and move at a pace that serves you and your body. The event will end with a 30 min sound-bath where you will be immersed in sound and vibrations from a variety of instruments. 
Sessions will be held outdoors on a level grassy surface. Mats provided. In case of inclement weather, session will be moved indoors. 
Participants can also connect to the rich history of Spadina by taking part in a tour of the historic house following the session.

fields.alt: Keke Chambers holds a yoga posture surrounded by musical bowls, crystals and other elements used in sound-bath.

Presenting the work of 5 women artists who meet monthly to share their work. 

The isolation of individual art practice is counter-balanced by their association with each other. Working in different media, the sensibility and leanings of each artist inform and enrich, while each remain very particular in their vision. Each artist moves individually between representation and abstraction, between internal and external, offering consistently thoughtful observation, detailed wonder and worry, and determination to question the work, its context in art, in the social and cultural realm, and in the spheres larger and smaller.

Marking a quarter-century of artistic excellence and community impact, Being Scene is a vital platform showcasing the work of artists with lived experiences of mental health and addiction.The artworks on display at this year’s juried exhibition include a diverse collection of painting, photography, digital media, installations, sculpture and video featuring 28 select artists. Gather for this immersive workshop and reflect deeply through an artistic journey inspired by the Sankofa Adinkra symbol, a powerful West African concept reminding us that it is never too late to return to the past to reclaim wisdom for the future. Enjoy a guided meditation and sound journey focused on the First Chakra (Root Chakra), supporting grounding, safety, and connection. Through the resonance of singing bowls and intentional breathwork, experience a gently guided state of presence that nurtures stability and embodied awareness. From this grounded space, explore artistic creation as a pathway to reconnect with personal history, cultural identity, and creative expression and aspects of self that are often overlooked in daily life. The Sankofa symbol serves as an anchor, encouraging reflection on ancestry, inherited wisdom, and the shared human experience beneath visible differences.

Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

value.event_description:
Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

How well can you read handwritten items? Come test your decoding skills as we explore several hundred years of handwritten words on items from Toronto Public Library’s Special Collections. 

The value of cursive writing has become a matter of debate as rapid technological changes make the need to put pen to paper increasingly rare. 

One area where the prominence of handwriting is undeniable is in archives of historical papers - explore this exhibition and see a variety of formats that researchers make use of such as personal letters, diaries, and notebooks as well as public documents, business records, and maps.

The debut of an exciting new Canadian play.

On the deck of a ship stands ‘The Atlantean,’ a single-seat submersible designed to withstand the deepest reaches of Earth’s oceans. Next to it stands Levin, whose dream of a research mission to the bottom of the ocean has become a reality in spite of questions surrounding his scientific views. The deeper he goes, and the darker it gets, the more dire his dive becomes, and the surer he gets that he is being stalked by something just out of sight…

A story of wonder, fear, and romance, this is the story of a scientist’s descent into a world where he will either shed light on one of the world’s last great mysteries, or become a part of it.

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections.

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

The only way to find your voice is to use it. In San Francisco, four artists and intellectuals wrestle with creativity, legacy, and the complexities of love and family. When they uncover the work of a Black queer feminist writer from the 1960s, her words ripple across time, intertwining their lives in unexpected ways. 

Bold and imaginative, Christina Anderson’s latest work explores the power of artistic expression and the lasting impact of those who dare to create. A story for dreamers and idealists alike, it challenges us to reconsider who gets remembered and who gets to define the future.

Written by Christina Anderson and directed by Mumbi Tindyebwa Otu.

Enjoy the world premiere of Karma by Aksam Alyousef, directed by Ash Knight, starring Basel Daoud, Zaynna Khalife, Andrew Iles, Tony Nash, and Christina Tannous. 

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. His Syrian mother, Karma, worries for his mental health, and forces him to dismiss the notion. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

A woman comes to terms with the fragility of her mental health while witnessing the demise of her partner through addiction, this is the everyday reality of living with and loving an addict.

Moving between fantasy and reality, past and present, and inspired by equine therapy, the play explores the deepening bond between a Horse and a Woman, and how they come together to negotiate their relationship, re-discover play and how they eventually heal each other in the process.

A high octane rollercoaster with stunning visuals and immersive soundscape, this experience is for anyone seeking a silver lining in the dark.

From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections. 

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

value.event_description:
Experience Buxtehude’s profound influence on Bach.

In 1705, the 20-year-old Johann Sebastian Bach journeyed 400 kilometres on foot from Arnstadt to Lübeck to meet and learn from the great composer Dietrich Buxtehude, then aged 70. During Bach’s three-month stay he would have experienced Buxtehude’s legendary Abendmusiken, or “Evening Concerts”, with their mix of sacred vocal and instrumental music presented in St. Mary’s Church.  

Our own special Abendmusik invites you to experience Buxtehude’s profound influence on Bach, and meet other musical travellers along the way: Johann Christoph Bach, Graupner, Doles, Reincken and Krebs. 

Come, refresh your spirit and soul!

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

A bold new international festival celebrating the global family of hammered dulcimers, brilliant instruments played by striking metal strings with delicate wooden mallets.

The festival brings together master musicians from Asia, the Middle East, and Europe for a vibrant program of performances, talks, and cultural exchange, led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri.

From the Persian santur and Indian santoor to the Chinese yangqin and European cimbalom, these instruments share a strikingly similar design and a centuries-spanning musical lineage. Though rooted in different traditions, they create a shared language of shimmering, expressive sound.

HAMMERED celebrates both this shared heritage and the distinct voices of each tradition, revealing how ancient instruments continue to inspire and evolve in the hands of today’s artists.

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. His Syrian mother, Karma, worries for his mental health, and forces him to dismiss the notion. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

The 2026 edition will include free community events and presentations of new work from nine artists in the Directors Lab, Playwrights Unit, Indigenous Arts Program, and Design Lab 2026 cohort: Kéïta Fournier-Pelletier, Jane-Leigh Jamieson, Suleekha Hirsi, Gwen Gabriella Caughell, Melissa Avalos, Nicci Pryce, Kobena Ampofo, Vandana Maharaj, and saysah.

"It's hard to believe that Paprika has been supporting young and emerging artists for a quarter of a century! Since its humble origins as a teen theatre festival operating out of Tarragon Theatre in 2001, Paprika has since evolved to be the launching pad for over 160 professional arts careers, with alumni including Zaiba Baig, Joelle Peters, Bea Pizano, and Mitchell Cushman”, said Amanda Lin, Artistic Producer.

The Yacht Rock Show Canada is an authentic tribute to the 70s and 80s Classic Smooth Rock Era that defined a generation.

 Experience an unforgettable musical voyage, dancing and listening to classic hits from artists including: Toto, Styx, The Doobie Brothers, Michael McDonald, Christopher Cross, Kenny Loggins, Steely Dan, Boz Scaggs, Player, Little River Band, Ambrosia.

The El Mocambo is a legendary live music and entertainment venue in Toronto, Canada, that has hosted countless world-famous artists since it opened in 1948, including The Rolling Stones, Elvis Costello, Blondie, The Ramones, and Stevie Ray Vaughan. The new El Mocambo features state-of-the-art sound and lighting, a recording studio, and multiple floors for events and performances, offering a modern, VIP live music experience while maintaining its historical significance.

value.event_description:
A woman comes to terms with the fragility of her mental health while witnessing the demise of her partner through addiction, this is the everyday reality of living with and loving an addict.

Moving between fantasy and reality, past and present, and inspired by equine therapy, the play explores the deepening bond between a Horse and a Woman, and how they come together to negotiate their relationship, re-discover play and how they eventually heal each other in the process.

A high octane rollercoaster with stunning visuals and immersive soundscape, this experience is for anyone seeking a silver lining in the dark.

The only way to find your voice is to use it. In San Francisco, four artists and intellectuals wrestle with creativity, legacy, and the complexities of love and family. When they uncover the work of a Black queer feminist writer from the 1960s, her words ripple across time, intertwining their lives in unexpected ways.

Written by Christina Anderson and directed by Mumbi Tindyebwa Otu.

value.event_description:
This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

value.event_description:
Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

value.event_description:
Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

When they uncover the work of a Black queer feminist writer from the 1960s, her words ripple across time, intertwining their lives in unexpected ways.

value.event_description:
From award-winning Ukrainian Canadian writer/director Andrew Kushnir, puzzle through a family history shaped by war and what gets carried forward into today’s battle.

After publishing a eulogy for his renowned watchmaker grandfather in a national newspaper, Andrew is confronted by an accusation in the comments section. The charge sends him on a 19,000-kilometre journey through Ukraine and Europe with daunting questions and the rare timepiece he's inherited. Retracing his grandfather’s footsteps as a soldier and immigrant, he unearths a family mythology that has astonishing implications for the present.

In a landscape where history is both weapon and wound, Andrew’s search pulls him deep into the stories of a shrinking Ukrainian village, into the fallout of Russia’s full-scale invasion and into the silence of the dead.

Originally featured at Lincoln Center, in New York City, this is a gripping new work on identity, legacy, and the slyness of memory.

A bold new international festival celebrating the global family of hammered dulcimers, brilliant instruments played by striking metal strings with delicate wooden mallets.

The festival brings together master musicians from Asia, the Middle East, and Europe for a vibrant program of performances, talks, and cultural exchange, led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri.

From the Persian santur and Indian santoor to the Chinese yangqin and European cimbalom, these instruments share a strikingly similar design and a centuries-spanning musical lineage. Though rooted in different traditions, they create a shared language of shimmering, expressive sound.

HAMMERED celebrates both this shared heritage and the distinct voices of each tradition, revealing how ancient instruments continue to inspire and evolve in the hands of today’s artists.

Enjoy the world premiere of Karma by Aksam Alyousef, directed by Ash Knight, starring Basel Daoud, Zaynna Khalife, Andrew Iles, Tony Nash, and Christina Tannous. 

The bonds of family, the trauma of civil war, the notion of forgiveness and how our circumstances shape us.

Set in 2012, Karma follows Adeeb, a young man born in Canada who believes that he lived a previous life in Syria. His Syrian mother, Karma, worries for his mental health, and forces him to dismiss the notion. Now an adult, Adeeb travels to Syria, forcing himself and his mother to confront their past and current lives.

A high octane rollercoaster with stunning visuals and immersive soundscape, this experience is for anyone seeking a silver lining in the dark.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

value.event_description: The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program® is backed by decades of research, yet is so simple and natural that parents easily gain skills and confidence to foster healthy relationships and give their children experiences that promote positive brain development, which peaks by the age of three and is largely set for life. All children’s early experiences mould their brains, and the primary caregiver provides most of those experiences. The caregiver’s choice of words, tone of voice, gestures, facial expressions, holding, and cuddling lay the neurological foundation for the child’s lifelong emotional, physical, and cognitive health. The Program prioritizes families in need of support and is always free.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections.

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.
