Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

Visit Smoke Signals x Reflections, an exhibition where photography, beadwork, sculpture and digital media serve as a guiding signal, broadcasting stories of identity, memory and reconnection. 

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.
 
Smoke Signals x Reflections is a safe and affirming space for two-spirit, Indigi-queer, and gender nonconforming artists.

A cheeky, heartfelt solo show about Nawaaz's journey of reclaiming his voice and cultural inheritance through learning tabla, a northern Indian percussion instrument. Twenty years of being a “coconut” has caught up to Nawaaz, who has crashed into a dual crisis of identity and faith. Divine intervention sends him a musical Guru, who guides him on a journey towards self-acceptance and love. 

Directed by Tiffany Wu, bol, brown boy, bol offers a rich musical landscape merging Indian classical music with 90s Bollywood nostalgia, grunge, rap and hip hop. Weaving storytelling with the rhythms of tabla, creator and performer Nawaaz speaks up about the impact of Canadian racism on his identity and shares his story of finding his way back to himself.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

She is currently artist-in-residence at both the Chicago Symphony Orchestra and London’s Wigmore Hall, and is co-founder and vice president of artistic partnerships of the AI-music initiative Deepmusic.AI. A cheeky, heartfelt solo show about Nawaaz's journey of reclaiming his voice and cultural inheritance through learning tabla, a northern Indian percussion instrument. Twenty years of being a “coconut” has caught up to Nawaaz, who has crashed into a dual crisis of identity and faith. Divine intervention sends him a musical Guru, who guides him on a journey towards self-acceptance and love. 

Directed by Tiffany Wu, bol, brown boy, bol offers a rich musical landscape merging Indian classical music with 90s Bollywood nostalgia, grunge, rap and hip hop. Weaving storytelling with the rhythms of tabla, creator and performer Nawaaz speaks up about the impact of Canadian racism on his identity and shares his story of finding his way back to himself.

Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

Don Murphy is a proud Irishman, a hopeless addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cockerel to be precise.

Over one fateful night, the feathered Oscar-winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience, from his big break, to his first bird-on-bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way, Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chickenkind and humankind.

Sold-out run and winner of Filipa Bragança Award at Edinburgh Fringe 2023.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” - Playbill

Presented as part of Canada Ireland Foundation’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival, which brings the best of Irish theatre to Toronto.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Comprising of 16 different artworks, that thread together elements of West African mask-making traditions, science fiction, geometric figures and interstellar vessels to create an amorphous futuristic tapestry. The interlacing of natural elements and the primary geometric forms often associated with LEGO® evoke an aesthetic that is at times haunting, futuristic and simultaneously traditional.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections. 

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Returning in 2026 we are proud to present our fourth iteration of this series, connecting Toronto with critically acclaimed International works that push the boundaries of live performance and cultural storytelling.

This year features BeyondTO returning artists, Wayqeycuna by Tiziano Cruz (Argentina) and Mark of a Woman by Chisato Minamimura (United Kingdom). These are two visionary artists whose work explores the intersections of identity, heritage, memory, and the human body. 

In Wayqeycuna, Tiziano Cruz draws from archival research and personal history and reflects on how racial hierarchies and systems of domination persist in a world reshaped by neoliberalism’s erasure of cultural and collective identities.

In Mark of a Woman, the personal histories and tattooing culture is explored and celebrated.

Audiences to experience the world through radically different perspectives, each one redefining how we connect across cultures, languages, and lived experience.

A cheeky, heartfelt solo show about Nawaaz's journey of reclaiming his voice and cultural inheritance through learning tabla, a northern Indian percussion instrument. Twenty years of being a “coconut” has caught up to Nawaaz, who has crashed into a dual crisis of identity and faith. Divine intervention sends him a musical Guru, who guides him on a journey towards self-acceptance and love. 

Directed by Tiffany Wu, bol, brown boy, bol offers a rich musical landscape merging Indian classical music with 90s Bollywood nostalgia, grunge, rap and hip hop. Weaving storytelling with the rhythms of tabla, creator and performer Nawaaz speaks up about the impact of Canadian racism on his identity and shares his story of finding his way back to himself.

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

Don Murphy is a proud Irishman, a hopeless addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cockerel to be precise.

Over one fateful night, the feathered Oscar-winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience, from his big break, to his first bird-on-bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way, Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chickenkind and humankind.

Sold-out run and winner of Filipa Bragança Award at Edinburgh Fringe 2023.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” - Playbill

Presented as part of Canada Ireland Foundation’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival, which brings the best of Irish theatre to Toronto.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

value.event_description:
Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

value.event_description:
Take advantage of this special opportunity to visit the restored interior of the historic schoolhouse.   

Zion Schoolhouse was built in 1869 and was designed to offer a basic education to the local children aged 6 to 13.  When it closed in 1955 the surrounding area was still mainly rural.  In the 1980s the schoolroom was restored to represent a 1910 period and to be used as a living history museum for visiting school classes.  

Drop in and try some of the old fashioned toys and schoolroom tools that would be in use in the early twentieth century and learn about the history of the schoolhouse.

fields.alt: Black and white photo of a one room schoolhouse with schoolchildren sitting in front

event_locations.location_notes: The Schoolhouse is at Finch Avenue East and Trudy Road.  There is limited parking south of the building.  From Finch Avenue drive south on Trudy Road, and turn right on Angus Drive.  There is a paved path from the parking lot to the schoolhouse.

value.event_description: At 20 hectares in size, Biidaasige Park is the largest public park to open in Toronto in over a generation. But what visitors might not know is that Biidaasige Park is also a critical and complex piece of climate-resilient infrastructure that is key to unlocking the first phase of the Port Lands revitalization. Explore the history of the Port Lands – from glaciation to waterfront revitalization – the decades of advocacy for a buried landscape, and the recent renaturalization of the Lower Don River as part of the broader renewal of this important place on Toronto’s waterfront.

fields.alt: A river and modern bridge against a blue sky.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Go behind the scenes with Toronto History Museums’ Collections staff on a guided tour of the third-floor fine art storage vault. Visitors will see the gallery’s specialized movable storage racks and highlights from the City of Toronto’s collection, including landscapes and large oil portraits of Toronto’s mayors from the past 180 years.

Staff will also be available on the second floor in the gallery to share the history of St. Lawrence Market and Toronto’s first City Hall, and to offer a preview of works in progress for the upcoming exhibition.

Vault tours run every hour from 10 am to 4 pm and last approximately 15 minutes. To sign up, please visit the Market Gallery on the second floor. Space is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Afternoon visitors are encouraged to arrive at least 30 minutes early to reserve a spot.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Returning in 2026 we are proud to present our fourth iteration of this series, connecting Toronto with critically acclaimed International works that push the boundaries of live performance and cultural storytelling.

This year features BeyondTO returning artists, Wayqeycuna by Tiziano Cruz (Argentina) and Mark of a Woman by Chisato Minamimura (United Kingdom). These are two visionary artists whose work explores the intersections of identity, heritage, memory, and the human body. 

In Wayqeycuna, Tiziano Cruz draws from archival research and personal history and reflects on how racial hierarchies and systems of domination persist in a world reshaped by neoliberalism’s erasure of cultural and collective identities.

In Mark of a Woman, the personal histories and tattooing culture is explored and celebrated.

Audiences to experience the world through radically different perspectives, each one redefining how we connect across cultures, languages, and lived experience.

Don Murphy is a proud Irishman, a hopeless addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cockerel to be precise.

Over one fateful night, the feathered Oscar-winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience, from his big break, to his first bird-on-bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way, Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chickenkind and humankind.

Sold-out run and winner of Filipa Bragança Award at Edinburgh Fringe 2023.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” - Playbill

Presented as part of Canada Ireland Foundation’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival, which brings the best of Irish theatre to Toronto.

An annual celebration bringing the best of contemporary Irish theatre to Toronto. Enjoy Canadian premieres of some of Ireland’s most captivating and contemporary theatre.

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. A cheeky, heartfelt solo show about Nawaaz's journey of reclaiming his voice and cultural inheritance through learning tabla, a northern Indian percussion instrument. Twenty years of being a “coconut” has caught up to Nawaaz, who has crashed into a dual crisis of identity and faith. Divine intervention sends him a musical Guru, who guides him on a journey towards self-acceptance and love. 

Directed by Tiffany Wu, bol, brown boy, bol offers a rich musical landscape merging Indian classical music with 90s Bollywood nostalgia, grunge, rap and hip hop. Weaving storytelling with the rhythms of tabla, creator and performer Nawaaz speaks up about the impact of Canadian racism on his identity and shares his story of finding his way back to himself.

value.event_description:
Don Murphy is a proud Irishman, a hopeless addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cockerel to be precise.

Over one fateful night, the feathered Oscar-winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience, from his big break, to his first bird-on-bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way, Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chickenkind and humankind.

Sold-out run and winner of Filipa Bragança Award at Edinburgh Fringe 2023.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” - Playbill

Presented as part of Canada Ireland Foundation’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival, which brings the best of Irish theatre to Toronto.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Take advantage of this special opportunity to visit the restored interior of the historic schoolhouse.   

Zion Schoolhouse was built in 1869 and was designed to offer a basic education to the local children aged 6 to 13.  When it closed in 1955 the surrounding area was still mainly rural.  In the 1980s the schoolroom was restored to represent a 1910 period and to be used as a living history museum for visiting school classes.  

Drop in and try some of the old fashioned toys and schoolroom tools that would be in use in the early twentieth century and learn about the history of the schoolhouse.

event_locations.location_notes: The Schoolhouse is at Finch Avenue East and Trudy Road.  There is limited parking south of the building.  From Finch Avenue drive south on Trudy Road, and turn right on Angus Drive.  There is a paved path from the parking lot to the schoolhouse.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

Don Murphy is a proud Irishman, a hopeless addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cockerel to be precise.

Over one fateful night, the feathered Oscar-winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience, from his big break, to his first bird-on-bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way, Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chickenkind and humankind.

Sold-out run and winner of Filipa Bragança Award at Edinburgh Fringe 2023.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” - Playbill

Presented as part of Canada Ireland Foundation’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival, which brings the best of Irish theatre to Toronto.

An annual celebration bringing the best of contemporary Irish theatre to Toronto. Enjoy Canadian premieres of some of Ireland’s most captivating and contemporary theatre. 

The festival kicks off with the one-of-a-kind, one-person show, CHICKEN. This award-winning production from Sunday’s Child Theatre had a sold-out run at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe Festival and exemplifies the originality of Ireland’s independent theatre scene. 

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

value.event_description:
A cheeky, heartfelt solo show about Nawaaz's journey of reclaiming his voice and cultural inheritance through learning tabla, a northern Indian percussion instrument. Twenty years of being a “coconut” has caught up to Nawaaz, who has crashed into a dual crisis of identity and faith. Divine intervention sends him a musical Guru, who guides him on a journey towards self-acceptance and love. 

Directed by Tiffany Wu, bol, brown boy, bol offers a rich musical landscape merging Indian classical music with 90s Bollywood nostalgia, grunge, rap and hip hop. Weaving storytelling with the rhythms of tabla, creator and performer Nawaaz speaks up about the impact of Canadian racism on his identity and shares his story of finding his way back to himself.

For Flamenco, "Tango" is a palo, a specific style of the art form. 

But for many people, tango might simply mean Argentine Tango...so what's the difference?

Both Argentine Tango and Flamenco originated in marginalized communities and immigrant cultures in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and are defined by their passion, melancholy, and improvisational nature.

Curious to learn more? Come experience it for yourself! 

Featuring Argentine Tango dancers Junko Mita Bodie and Pedro De Oliveira, alongside violinist Aparna Halpé and the Toronto Tango Community Orchestra, with all music arranged by Elena Losseva.

Joining them for flamenco are acclaimed local musicians Ana Lía and Nicolas Hernandez, with flamenco dance by Kiyo Asaoka. Don't miss this exciting and unique performance!

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

All children’s early experiences mould their brains, and the primary caregiver provides most of those experiences. The caregiver’s choice of words, tone of voice, gestures, facial expressions, holding, and cuddling lay the neurological foundation for the child’s lifelong emotional, physical, and cognitive health. The Program prioritizes families in need of support and is always free.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections.

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Visit Smoke Signals x Reflections, an exhibition where photography, beadwork, sculpture and digital media serve as a guiding signal, broadcasting stories of identity, memory and reconnection. 

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.

An annual celebration bringing the best of contemporary Irish theatre to Toronto. Enjoy Canadian premieres of some of Ireland’s most captivating and contemporary theatre. 

The festival kicks off with the one-of-a-kind, one-person show, CHICKEN. This award-winning production from Sunday’s Child Theatre had a sold-out run at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe Festival and exemplifies the originality of Ireland’s independent theatre scene. 

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

value.event_description:
Danny O’Mahony has dedicated his life to the mastery of his instrument as well as to the preservation and performance of Irish traditional music.

 Now, after 40 years of breathing life into centuries-old tunes to honour the memory of those who have come before him, this walking repository is finally taking a breath, a moment to stop and consider what this lifelong dedication has cost him.

 Bellow is a new theatre performance exploring the weight of tradition, the capriciousness of memory and the artist’s need to express their true self.

value.event_description:
This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

fields.alt: Abstract painting with various geometric shapes in a grey beige colour scheme.

An annual celebration bringing the best of contemporary Irish theatre to Toronto. Enjoy Canadian premieres of some of Ireland’s most captivating and contemporary theatre. 

The festival kicks off with the one-of-a-kind, one-person show, CHICKEN. This award-winning production from Sunday’s Child Theatre had a sold-out run at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe Festival and exemplifies the originality of Ireland’s independent theatre scene. 

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

Danny O’Mahony has dedicated his life to the mastery of his instrument as well as to the preservation and performance of Irish traditional music.

 Now, after 40 years of breathing life into centuries-old tunes to honour the memory of those who have come before him, this walking repository is finally taking a breath, a moment to stop and consider what this lifelong dedication has cost him.

 Bellow is a new theatre performance exploring the weight of tradition, the capriciousness of memory and the artist’s need to express their true self.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections. 

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Our season finale at Koerner Hall salutes this uplifting spirit with music by Ludwig van Beethoven and Joseph Bologne, composers who embraced change and challenged the status quo.     

A trailblazer in his own right, the renowned Japanese-American violinist Shunsuke Sato makes his Tafelmusik debut directing these performances. Concertmaster of Concerto Köln and former Artistic Leader of the Netherlands Bach Society, Sato is known for performances that push the envelope and “dig deeper into his instrument” (Gramophone). 

Leading the orchestra from the violin, Sato directs Beethoven’s Symphony no. 3, “Eroica,” a work that profoundly changed the symphonic form while staying true to the composer’s ethos. Don’t miss your chance to experience this!

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

value.event_description: Gathering multiple histories, geographies and cultural lineages within a shared space, these five immigrant women artists reflect the World in a City – where distant homelands, memories and identities coexist and take root. Each artist has experienced displacement and, through their work, connect lived realities with the fragility and resilience of flowers. By situating women’s stories alongside flowers as equally independent yet interwoven beings, this project foregrounds cycles of rupture and renewal, resilience and rebirth. Featuring works by Arshin Agashteh, Maryam (Sora) Kheiry, Ebru Winegrad, Golbahar Hassanabadi and Gizem Candan.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

In celebration of the CONTACT Photography Festival, we are pleased to present a photography exhibition “The Water Between Us” by Meaghan Ogilvie.

This exhibition presents a captivating retrospective of Meaghan Ogilvie’s work, tracing more than a decade of her artistic journey. Known for her award-winning underwater photography, Ogilvie explores the delicate relationship between humans and water through imagery that is both ethereal and deeply rooted in environmental awareness. Featuring highlights from international exhibitions, artist residencies, and major public art commissions, the show reflects the evolution of her practice, from early explorations to her most celebrated projects. Together, these works offer an intimate look at an artist whose lens transforms water into a powerful, poetic medium for connection, memory, and reflection.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

value.event_description:
Emerge from winter hibernation and welcome in the spring energy this May. Explore the elements (Earth, Fire, Water & Air) through an open level vinyasa yoga flow and sound-bath meditation in a four-week series. Join Keke Chambers, a multi-disciplinary artist, facilitator, and healer with over two decades of movement experience. Each week you’ll explore the elements by infusing movement with connection to each week’s theme. With an emphasis on accessibility and inclusion, you’ll be guided to connect to your own inner teacher and move at a pace that serves you and your body. The event will end with a 30 min sound-bath where you will be immersed in sound and vibrations from a variety of instruments. 
Sessions will be held outdoors on a level grassy surface. Mats provided. In case of inclement weather, session will be moved indoors. 
Participants can also connect to the rich history of Spadina by taking part in a tour of the historic house following the session.

fields.alt: Keke Chambers holds a yoga posture surrounded by musical bowls, crystals and other elements used in sound-bath.

A community-led arts and heavy music festival, the first of its kind in the city! 

Founded by two lifelong friends, Toronto-based concert promoter Denholm Whale and KW Campol of music management company Mythos and the Perpetual Flame Ministries record label/art house. 

Drawing inspiration from European festival stalwarts like Roadburn, Supersonic, and Amplifest, we're focused on heavy music as an ethos of collective catharsis more than a dedication to one specific metal subgenre. From burgeoning artists, to favorites you never thought would reunite, to one-off full album sets, a heavily curated and meticulously planned lineup is the festival’s key component.

value.event_description:
Visit Smoke Signals x Reflections, an exhibition where photography, beadwork, sculpture and digital media serve as a guiding signal, broadcasting stories of identity, memory and reconnection. 

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.
 
Smoke Signals x Reflections is a safe and affirming space for two-spirit, Indigi-queer, and gender nonconforming artists.

Come to the biggest beatbox event North America has ever seen!

Reuniting the Official Canadian Beatbox Championships and the internationally renowned Great North Battle into one landmark all‑ages festival!

For the first time ever, both championships will run under one roof, welcoming top vocal percussionists from Canada and around the world for three days. 

The festival will showcase elite competitors from Canada, France, the United States, Japan, the UK, Mexico, Chile, and Hong Kong, including nationally ranked artists and returning champions across solo and loopstation categories. The entire weekend is open to all ages, making it a unique opportunity for families and music fans to experience world‑class live vocal workshops, battles and performances.
This historic weekend is presented in partnership with SING!

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

An annual celebration bringing the best of contemporary Irish theatre to Toronto. Enjoy Canadian premieres of some of Ireland’s most captivating and contemporary theatre. 

The festival kicks off with the one-of-a-kind, one-person show, CHICKEN. This award-winning production from Sunday’s Child Theatre had a sold-out run at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe Festival and exemplifies the originality of Ireland’s independent theatre scene. 

Next, from Dublin’s boundary-breaking Brokentalkers comes BELLOW, a new theatre performance exploring the beauty and weight of keeping traditional Irish music alive, featuring expert accordionist Danny O’Mahony. Then comes an extraordinary adaptation of the story of Ulysses for children and adults alike. In Branar’s YOU’LL SEE, James Joyce’s epic story is reinvented for ages 8 and up.

Our season finale at Koerner Hall salutes this uplifting spirit with music by Ludwig van Beethoven and Joseph Bologne, composers who embraced change and challenged the status quo.     

A trailblazer in his own right, the renowned Japanese-American violinist Shunsuke Sato makes his Tafelmusik debut directing these performances. Concertmaster of Concerto Köln and former Artistic Leader of the Netherlands Bach Society, Sato is known for performances that push the envelope and “dig deeper into his instrument” (Gramophone). 

Leading the orchestra from the violin, Sato directs Beethoven’s Symphony no. 3, “Eroica,” a work that profoundly changed the symphonic form while staying true to the composer’s ethos. Don’t miss your chance to experience this!

Danny O’Mahony has dedicated his life to the mastery of his instrument as well as to the preservation and performance of Irish traditional music.

 Now, after 40 years of breathing life into centuries-old tunes to honour the memory of those who have come before him, this walking repository is finally taking a breath, a moment to stop and consider what this lifelong dedication has cost him.

 Bellow is a new theatre performance exploring the weight of tradition, the capriciousness of memory and the artist’s need to express their true self.
