value.event_description:
This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

value.event_description:
Witness the compelling works of Karolina Kuras' ballet photography and Ted Belton's fashion photography.

Both with special eyes for movement, texture, and contrast, their work creates windows into the souls of their subjects, and the auras underneath honest moments better translated visually than with words. Karolina and Ted's contemporary styles naturally complement each other, capturing discipline and grace in visual conversation. Together, their photographs reveal how fashion and dance are connected practices, through their vulnerable yet performative natures. This exhibition is a Photo Diary of Karolina and Ted’s photography practices, experimenting with human expression, creative process, and print materials.

value.event_description:
Examine the visual and material tension between wilderness and human control along Scarborough’s shoreline park system. Using traditional photographic techniques, the work moves from representational landscape toward abstraction, tracing how natural forces and urban intervention shape one another over time. The project draws from repeated visits to shoreline parks, beaches, and wooded areas along the bluffs. 

About the Artist
Chris is a Toronto-based photographer. Contemplative observation with a strong graphic sensibility for image making, have come to represent his photographic style. His personal work can be found in corporate and private collections throughout North America and Europe.

value.event_description:
Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

value.event_description: Gathering multiple histories, geographies and cultural lineages within a shared space, these five immigrant women artists reflect the World in a City – where distant homelands, memories and identities coexist and take root. Each artist has experienced displacement and, through their work, connect lived realities with the fragility and resilience of flowers. By situating women’s stories alongside flowers as equally independent yet interwoven beings, this project foregrounds cycles of rupture and renewal, resilience and rebirth. Featuring works by Arshin Agashteh, Maryam (Sora) Kheiry, Ebru Winegrad, Golbahar Hassanabadi and Gizem Candan.

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

Our season finale at Koerner Hall salutes this uplifting spirit with music by Ludwig van Beethoven and Joseph Bologne, composers who embraced change and challenged the status quo.     

A trailblazer in his own right, the renowned Japanese-American violinist Shunsuke Sato makes his Tafelmusik debut directing these performances. Concertmaster of Concerto Köln and former Artistic Leader of the Netherlands Bach Society, Sato is known for performances that push the envelope and “dig deeper into his instrument” (Gramophone). 

Leading the orchestra from the violin, Sato directs Beethoven’s Symphony no. 3, “Eroica,” a work that profoundly changed the symphonic form while staying true to the composer’s ethos. Don’t miss your chance to experience this!

A community-led arts and heavy music festival, the first of its kind in the city! 

Founded by two lifelong friends, Toronto-based concert promoter Denholm Whale and KW Campol of music management company Mythos and the Perpetual Flame Ministries record label/art house. 

Drawing inspiration from European festival stalwarts like Roadburn, Supersonic, and Amplifest, we're focused on heavy music as an ethos of collective catharsis more than a dedication to one specific metal subgenre. From burgeoning artists, to favorites you never thought would reunite, to one-off full album sets, a heavily curated and meticulously planned lineup is the festival’s key component.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

value.event_description: The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program® is backed by decades of research, yet is so simple and natural that parents easily gain skills and confidence to foster healthy relationships and give their children experiences that promote positive brain development, which peaks by the age of three and is largely set for life. All children’s early experiences mould their brains, and the primary caregiver provides most of those experiences. The caregiver’s choice of words, tone of voice, gestures, facial expressions, holding, and cuddling lay the neurological foundation for the child’s lifelong emotional, physical, and cognitive health. The Program prioritizes families in need of support and is always free.

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections.

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

See Toronto in a brand-new light.

British artist Liz West creates sculptural works using coloured acrylic, mirrored surfaces, and refracted light. Designed to respond to the movement of the sun, the installations shift throughout the day: grids of coloured panels glow against glass facades, mirrored elements reflect and multiply surrounding architecture, and translucent walls scatter prismatic colour into the space around them.

These are not static sculptures but responsive environments, works that use daylight as a material. As the light changes, familiar buildings and public spaces are transformed, turning marble, glass, and steel into luminous, layered, and unexpectedly playful experiences.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

value.event_description:
I slap and slide paint from the base of a canvas and move upward with my palette knife. 

Unrefined segments of various shades and colour rock and roll, lines intercept blocks and many go beyond the forms they touch. A rhythmic figure appears surrounded by a simple neutral background.  

The figure is a dancer. It's limbs flail, forms jump or twist and the body of my loosely composed figure vibrates with the music it hears. The subject moves alone, unaware that viewers are watching. 

My abstract landscapes involve a dialogue or relationship between areas of intensity or excitement on the canvas and space. The many times I have driven past Outaouais fields and inland roads near Mont Jolie, Qc. have left their imprint. While still using geometric forms, the abstract landscapes are based on nature.

Visit Smoke Signals x Reflections, an exhibition where photography, beadwork, sculpture and digital media serve as a guiding signal, broadcasting stories of identity, memory and reconnection. 

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.
 
Smoke Signals x Reflections is a safe and affirming space for two-spirit, Indigi-queer, and gender nonconforming artists.

value.event_description:
You are invited into an imperial space overtaken by plant life, where movement, sound, and space emerge beyond human logic. In layers of kin, performers move in kinship with moss, yarrow, clover, and oak to explore the connection between humans and the more-than-human world.

Unfolding in close proximity to the audience, the choreography emphasizes attentiveness and shared presence, allowing movement, sound, and space to shape the performance in real time. The work favours quiet accumulation over spectacle, revealing patterns of connection, resilience, and coexistence as the dancers move together across the space, creating a post-imperial ballroom utopia.

Choreographed by Angela Vitovec the piece continues Vitovec’s exploration of plant consciousness and interdependence, following earlier works Sammal/Moss and Mossbelly.

Content warning: may include nudity.﻿

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

Attend the world premiere of American Devotion, a play set at Marilyn Monroe’s home at the height of McCarthyism, which has found unexpected relevance in the time of Trump. 

American Devotion takes us back to 1957 and the Connecticut farmhouse shared by Marilyn Monroe and her celebrated playwright husband, Arthur Miller. In this fictional version of events, Norman Mailer has successfully wangled a coveted invitation for cocktails with the reclusive couple. With McCarthyism running rampant, Miller has been called to testify before the House of Un-American Activities Committee adding further strain to an already besieged marriage. Mailer storms into this delicate situation ready to do battle and claim his prize at any cost but Monroe has plans of her own.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

value.event_description:
See Toronto in a brand-new light.

British artist Liz West creates sculptural works using coloured acrylic, mirrored surfaces, and refracted light. Designed to respond to the movement of the sun, the installations shift throughout the day: grids of coloured panels glow against glass facades, mirrored elements reflect and multiply surrounding architecture, and translucent walls scatter prismatic colour into the space around them.

These are not static sculptures but responsive environments, works that use daylight as a material. As the light changes, familiar buildings and public spaces are transformed, turning marble, glass, and steel into luminous, layered, and unexpectedly playful experiences.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

value.event_description:
Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

value.event_description: Gathering multiple histories, geographies and cultural lineages within a shared space, these five immigrant women artists reflect the World in a City – where distant homelands, memories and identities coexist and take root. Each artist has experienced displacement and, through their work, connect lived realities with the fragility and resilience of flowers. By situating women’s stories alongside flowers as equally independent yet interwoven beings, this project foregrounds cycles of rupture and renewal, resilience and rebirth. Featuring works by Arshin Agashteh, Maryam (Sora) Kheiry, Ebru Winegrad, Golbahar Hassanabadi and Gizem Candan.

You are invited into an imperial space overtaken by plant life, where movement, sound, and space emerge beyond human logic. In layers of kin, performers move in kinship with moss, yarrow, clover, and oak to explore the connection between humans and the more-than-human world.

Unfolding in close proximity to the audience, the choreography emphasizes attentiveness and shared presence, allowing movement, sound, and space to shape the performance in real time. The work favours quiet accumulation over spectacle, revealing patterns of connection, resilience, and coexistence as the dancers move together across the space, creating a post-imperial ballroom utopia.

Choreographed by Angela Vitovec the piece continues Vitovec’s exploration of plant consciousness and interdependence, following earlier works Sammal/Moss and Mossbelly.

Content warning: may include nudity.﻿

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

Attend the world premiere of American Devotion, a play set at Marilyn Monroe’s home at the height of McCarthyism, which has found unexpected relevance in the time of Trump. 

American Devotion takes us back to 1957 and the Connecticut farmhouse shared by Marilyn Monroe and her celebrated playwright husband, Arthur Miller. In this fictional version of events, Norman Mailer has successfully wangled a coveted invitation for cocktails with the reclusive couple. With McCarthyism running rampant, Miller has been called to testify before the House of Un-American Activities Committee adding further strain to an already besieged marriage. Mailer storms into this delicate situation ready to do battle and claim his prize at any cost but Monroe has plans of her own.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

See Toronto in a brand-new light.

British artist Liz West creates sculptural works using coloured acrylic, mirrored surfaces, and refracted light. Designed to respond to the movement of the sun, the installations shift throughout the day: grids of coloured panels glow against glass facades, mirrored elements reflect and multiply surrounding architecture, and translucent walls scatter prismatic colour into the space around them.

These are not static sculptures but responsive environments, works that use daylight as a material. As the light changes, familiar buildings and public spaces are transformed, turning marble, glass, and steel into luminous, layered, and unexpectedly playful experiences.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Trace the overlooked spaces of Scarborough, a Toronto district often shaped by misconceptions. Returning to the place where she grew up, Jennifer Lee reconnects with its communities and terrain, uncovering moments of beauty while observing neighbourhoods in transition.

About the Artist
Jennifer Lee is a Toronto-based photographer focused on candid and street photography that captures the evolving dynamics of public spaces and community life. Her work explores themes of identity, belonging, and the quiet narratives of everyday moments. She collaborates with grassroots organizations to document the stories of growing communities, using photography as a tool for storytelling and social connection. Jennifer's practice reflects a commitment to accessible, socially relevant art that invites viewers to see the familiar in new ways.

The Parent-Child Mother Goose Program is an organization with over twenty years of experience dedicated to sharing the power of rhymes, songs, and stories with parents and their children, from newborns to age four. It aims to strengthen the bond between parents and children, enhance developmental skills in children, and build supportive community connections. 

Why is the Parent-Child Mother Goose Program important?
The program emphasizes that the bond between parent and child is essential. It provides practical tools like rhymes, songs, and stories that can be easily integrated into daily life. This helps parents create a joyful and stimulating environment, leading to stronger connections, improved communication skills, and positive family patterns. It also aims to prevent isolation and promote mental and physical well-being.

value.event_description: Gathering multiple histories, geographies and cultural lineages within a shared space, these five immigrant women artists reflect the World in a City – where distant homelands, memories and identities coexist and take root. Each artist has experienced displacement and, through their work, connect lived realities with the fragility and resilience of flowers. By situating women’s stories alongside flowers as equally independent yet interwoven beings, this project foregrounds cycles of rupture and renewal, resilience and rebirth. Featuring works by Arshin Agashteh, Maryam (Sora) Kheiry, Ebru Winegrad, Golbahar Hassanabadi and Gizem Candan.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

Curated by Jesse King, the exhibit shares pieces from City of Toronto’s Fine Art and Artifact Collection, including the photographic series The Emergence of a Legend by Kent Monkman as well as contemporary art by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, Jake Kimble, Kay Nadjiwon, Kikki Guerard, Megan Feheley and Melissa Johns. Expect bold visuals, self-discovery, and personal storytelling.
 
Smoke Signals x Reflections is a safe and affirming space for two-spirit, Indigi-queer, and gender nonconforming artists.

Enjoy the all-Canadian production of this three-time 2009 Tony Award winner, and the 2010 Pulitzer Prize winner. This is an electrifying and poignant depiction of a family in crisis trying to overcome the past. 

They're the perfect suburban family.Dad's an architect, brother and sister are acing their classes, and Mom's keeping them all together. There's just one small detail nobody wants to acknowledge, Mom's been battling bipolar disorder and delusional episodes for 16 years. Next to Normal is a compassionate look into how a family copes when mental health verges on the sublime.

Directed by Anthony Goncharov, Next To Normal will star April Rebecca as Diana, Taylor Long as Dan, Aveleigh Keller as Natalie, Christopher Lyon as Gabe, Samel Sunil as Henry, and Mich Anger as Dr Madden/Dr Fine. With book and lyrics by Brian Yorkey and music by Tom Kitt.

Attend the world premiere of American Devotion, a play set at Marilyn Monroe’s home at the height of McCarthyism, which has found unexpected relevance in the time of Trump. 

American Devotion takes us back to 1957 and the Connecticut farmhouse shared by Marilyn Monroe and her celebrated playwright husband, Arthur Miller. In this fictional version of events, Norman Mailer has successfully wangled a coveted invitation for cocktails with the reclusive couple. With McCarthyism running rampant, Miller has been called to testify before the House of Un-American Activities Committee adding further strain to an already besieged marriage. Mailer storms into this delicate situation ready to do battle and claim his prize at any cost but Monroe has plans of her own.

This groundbreaking original exhibition explores the profound connection between Japanese objects and the human sense of touch, known as "shokkan",a vital element in the creation and appreciation of Japanese art. Transcending the tactile sensations felt at the fingertips, shokkan is the combination of memories, language, and other senses like sight and sound. 

This exhibition showcases over 100 objects. From the intricate texture of a matcha tea bowl to the “imagined touch” of a woodblock print, be inspired by the exquisite and innovative craftsmanship through encounters with touchable objects and hands-on experiences that allow you to fully appreciate Japanese art.

See Toronto in a brand-new light.

British artist Liz West creates sculptural works using coloured acrylic, mirrored surfaces, and refracted light. Designed to respond to the movement of the sun, the installations shift throughout the day: grids of coloured panels glow against glass facades, mirrored elements reflect and multiply surrounding architecture, and translucent walls scatter prismatic colour into the space around them.

These are not static sculptures but responsive environments, works that use daylight as a material. As the light changes, familiar buildings and public spaces are transformed, turning marble, glass, and steel into luminous, layered, and unexpectedly playful experiences.

Trace the overlooked spaces of Scarborough, a Toronto district often shaped by misconceptions. Returning to the place where she grew up, Jennifer Lee reconnects with its communities and terrain, uncovering moments of beauty while observing neighbourhoods in transition.

About the Artist
Jennifer Lee is a Toronto-based photographer focused on candid and street photography that captures the evolving dynamics of public spaces and community life. Her work explores themes of identity, belonging, and the quiet narratives of everyday moments. She collaborates with grassroots organizations to document the stories of growing communities, using photography as a tool for storytelling and social connection. Jennifer's practice reflects a commitment to accessible, socially relevant art that invites viewers to see the familiar in new ways.

Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

Visit us to discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, archives, and paintings pulled from the City of Toronto's permanent collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.

Established in 1976, the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has served the local community for 50 years. Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery has presented more than 500 exhibitions and continues to nurture emerging talent, spotlight established artists and celebrate creativity at the community level. To celebrate this milestone, the City of Toronto’s Arts and Culture Services have created an exhibition that honours the past, celebrates the present, and looks forward to the future of the gallery.

Art. Culture. Science.

This groundbreaking exhibition challenges long-held narratives, presenting a balanced, research-driven examination of the cultural, historical, and scientific significance of psychedelics. 

Through artworks, objects, botanical specimens, and interactive experiences, enjoy a rich and expansive journey shaped by extensive consultation and thoughtful storytelling. Confronting a subject long surrounded by taboo, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with fresh, thought-provoking perspectives, reflecting on what psychedelics have meant across time and what they may come to represent in the future.
